query: How does resolution time vary by agent and issue type?

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: This is simply the focus variable expressed in hours (with some erroneous negative values). It restates resolution_time rather than providing an external, associational variable to segment on. As a continuous, fine-grained measure it cannot serve as a grouping dimension against the focus.

per_column.name: issue_type_category
per_column.rationale: Provides well-separated, interpretable categories (Network, Database, Software, Hardware) with meaningful non-degenerate distribution. Directly answers the 'by issue type' part of the query and supports grouped comparison of resolution_time across categories.

judge.rationale: Only one of the two added columns realises the EDA claim. issue_type_category is a strong, interpretable segmentation variable enabling comparison of resolution time across issue types. However, resolution_time_hours merely restates the focus variable and adds no relational information; it also contains invalid negative values. The query also asks about variation 'by agent', but no agent-related segmentation column was added (agent info exists only in the original table). As a set, the additions partially support interpretable relationship discovery but leave a key requested dimension uncovered and include a redundant restatement.
